cs.title: Contoso Financial Services Multi-Region Migration
cs.overview: Contoso Financial Services is a global banking organization migrating its core financial processing applications and databases from on-premises datacenters to Microsoft Azure. Contoso operates primarily in Europe and North America and must strictly comply with EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) data sovereignty mandates.
cs.businessRequirements:
1. High Availability: Core transactional API gateways must maintain a 99.99% uptime SLA.
2. Compliance & Sovereignty: All European customer PII data must remain strictly stored in EU Azure Regions.
3. Cost Optimization: Non-production environments (dev/test) must utilize cost-reduced VM pricing models, while production infrastructure uses 3-year Reserved Instance commitments.
4. Disaster Recovery: Business continuity plans require cross-region disaster recovery for all primary databases.
cs.technicalRequirements:
1. In-Memory SAP Databases: The core transactional database requires up to 2 TB of RAM.
2. High-Speed Compute: Batch calculation engines require high CPU clock speeds for fast execution.
3. Infrastructure as Code (IaC): All infrastructure deployments must be automated using Bicep templates integrated into CI/CD pipelines.
4. Security & Governance: Governance policies must be uniformly inherited across all child subscriptions.
cs.existingEnvironment: Current environment consists of on-premises VMware vSphere ESXi clusters, legacy Microsoft SQL Server clusters, and custom Bash deployment scripts.

questions.title: CS1: Select VM Family for SAP HANA
questions.prompt: Based on Contoso Technical Requirements, which Virtual Machine series should be selected to host the core in-memory SAP database requiring up to 2 TB of RAM?

options.text: E-Series or M-Series (Memory-Optimized)
F-Series (Compute-Optimized)
B-Series (Burstable CPU)
N-Series (GPU-Enabled)

questions.explanation: E-Series and M-Series VMs provide high memory-to-CPU ratios ideal for large in-memory databases like SAP HANA.

questions.title: CS1: SLA Model for 99.99%
questions.prompt: To satisfy Contoso Business Requirement for a 99.99% uptime SLA for core transactional API gateways, how should the Virtual Machines be deployed?

options.text: Across two or more Availability Zones in the same Azure region.
Inside a single Availability Set using Standard HDD disks.
As a single standalone VM using Standard SSD storage.
Inside an unmanaged storage account container.

questions.explanation: Multi-zone deployments across Availability Zones provide Azure 99.99% VM uptime SLA.

questions.title: CS1: Scope for Policy Inheritance
questions.prompt: At which architectural level should Contoso apply Azure Policies to guarantee uniform inheritance across all European child subscriptions?

options.text: Management Group Level
Resource Group Level
Subnet Level
Local Client Laptop Level

questions.explanation: Management Groups provide a scope of governance above subscriptions, allowing Azure Policy assignments to inherit down the hierarchy.

questions.title: CS1: Declarative IaC Deployment Tool
questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Infrastructure as Code (IaC) language meets Contoso requirement for automated, declarative environment deployments that compile into ARM templates?

options.text: Bicep
Python Scripting
Bash Shell
HTML5 Web Forms

questions.explanation: Bicep is Microsoft declarative domain-specific language (DSL) for authoring Azure infrastructure that compiles to ARM JSON.

questions.title: CS1: Regional Pairs Distance Requirement
questions.prompt: How far apart are paired Azure regions typically located to support Contoso cross-region disaster recovery requirements?

options.text: At least 300 miles apart.
10 meters apart.
Always in different hemispheres.
Exactly 1 mile apart.

questions.explanation: Azure Regional Pairs are separated by at least 300 miles where possible to protect against regional outages.

questions.title: CS1: Cost Optimization Strategies
questions.prompt: Which TWO cost optimization strategies align with Contoso requirements for non-production and production VM workloads? (Select TWO)

options.text: Using Azure Reserved VM Instances (RI) for 1-year or 3-year production commitments.
Using Azure Spot VMs or Burstable B-Series for dev/test environments.
Running all VMs at 100% CPU utilization 24/7 without stopping.
Deleting the billing account from the Azure portal.

questions.explanation: Reserved Instances offer up to 72% savings for production workloads, while Spot/B-Series optimize dev/test costs.

questions.title: CS1: VM Provisioning Child Components
questions.prompt: When Contoso provisions a new Virtual Machine compute instance, which TWO child resources are automatically created? (Select TWO)

options.text: Network Interface (NIC) attached to a Virtual Network Subnet.
Managed OS Disk storing the operating system.
Physical fiber optic cable delivered to the local office.
Azure Synapse Analytics dedicated SQL pool.

questions.explanation: Deploying an Azure VM provisions underlying resources: Virtual Machine instance, NIC, and Managed OS Disk.

questions.title: CS1: Azure Resource Manager Characteristics
questions.prompt: Which TWO statements correctly describe the central role of Azure Resource Manager (ARM) in Contoso deployment? (Select TWO)

options.text: Provides a unified management REST API layer for creating, updating, and deleting resources.
Authenticates and routes all requests initiated from Azure Portal, CLI, PowerShell, and Bicep.
Serves as an antivirus scanner installed on client laptops.
Physically manufactures server chassis inside datacenters.

questions.explanation: ARM is the central management layer for authentication, access control, and declarative resource orchestration.

questions.title: CS1: Availability Zone Features
questions.prompt: Which TWO statements accurately describe the physical characteristics of Azure Availability Zones? (Select TWO)

options.text: Each zone consists of physically separate datacenters with independent power, cooling, and networking.
Protect applications and data from datacenter facility failures.
Require connecting all servers to 4G cellular dongles.
Are only available inside A-series virtual machines.

questions.explanation: Availability Zones feature physically isolated datacenter buildings with redundant power and cooling.

questions.title: CS1: Infrastructure as Code Benefits
questions.prompt: Which TWO benefits will Contoso gain by adopting Bicep Infrastructure as Code (IaC)? (Select TWO)

options.text: Idempotency & Consistency: Ensures dev, test, and prod environments remain identical without configuration drift.
Automation & Speed: Enables rapid, repeatable deployments integrated into CI/CD DevOps pipelines.
Automatically increases home internet connection speed.
Eliminates the requirement for user authentication passwords.

questions.explanation: IaC provides repeatable, automated, consistent environment deployments.

questions.title: CS1: Match Contoso Workloads to VM Series
questions.prompt: Match each Contoso workload requirement to its optimal Azure Virtual Machine family series.

targets.label: SAP HANA in-memory database requiring up to 2 TB of RAM.
High-speed batch calculation engine requiring fast clock speed CPUs.
Dev/Test web environment with low baseline usage and periodic traffic bursts.
High-performance computing scientific simulations requiring InfiniBand networking.

questions.explanation: E = Memory Optimized, F = Compute Optimized, B = Burstable, H = HPC.

questions.title: CS1: Match Storage Tiers to Workloads
questions.prompt: Match each Managed Disk storage tier to Contoso target database workload.

targets.label: Sub-millisecond latency database storage for mission-critical transactional engines.
Production SQL Server databases requiring high IOPS and single-digit ms latency.
Light dev/test web server OS disks.
Non-critical cold backup files and archive storage.

questions.explanation: Ultra Disk = sub-ms; Premium SSD = Production SQL; Standard SSD = Dev/Test; Standard HDD = Cold backup.

questions.title: CS1: Match Management Tools to Use Cases
questions.prompt: Match each Azure management tool to Contoso usage scenario.

targets.label: Web-based GUI console for visual monitoring and dashboard customization.
Cross-platform CLI tool using az <group> <action> commands.
Task automation framework using Verb-Noun cmdlets (e.g. New-AzVM).
Declarative IaC files integrated into CI/CD pipelines.

questions.explanation: Portal = GUI, CLI = az commands, PowerShell = Verb-Noun, Bicep = Declarative IaC.

questions.title: CS1: Match Physical Architecture Levels
questions.prompt: Match each physical architecture boundary to its definition.

targets.label: Latency-defined perimeter containing datacenters linked by a dedicated fiber network.
Physically isolated datacenter with independent power, cooling, and networking.
Two regions in the same geography paired 300+ miles apart for DR.
Discrete market containing regions that preserve data residency compliance.

questions.explanation: Region, Zone, Pair, Geography physical hierarchy.

questions.title: CS1: Match Resource Lock Types
questions.prompt: Match each Azure Resource Lock type to its enforcement behavior.

targets.label: Allows authorized users to read and modify a resource, but prevents deletion.
Prevents authorized users from deleting or modifying a resource.
Inherits lock protections down to all child subscriptions.
Applies lock protections across all resource groups in a subscription.

questions.explanation: CanNotDelete allows edits but blocks deletion; ReadOnly blocks both edits and deletion.

questions.title: CS1: TF - Resource Group Deletion
questions.prompt: True or False: Deleting an Azure Resource Group in Contoso subscription automatically deletes all underlying virtual machines contained within it.
questions.explanation: Deleting a Resource Group deletes all child resources contained within that group as part of lifecycle cleanup.

questions.title: CS1: TF - Resource Group Location
questions.prompt: True or False: Contoso can deploy Virtual Machines physically located in Europe inside a Resource Group whose metadata location is set to East US.
questions.explanation: Resources inside a Resource Group do not have to reside in the same physical region as the Resource Group metadata location.

questions.title: CS1: TF - Fault Domains vs Update Domains
questions.prompt: True or False: Fault Domains (FD) group Virtual Machines together so they can be rebooted simultaneously during planned platform updates.
questions.explanation: False. Update Domains (UD) manage planned platform reboots; Fault Domains (FD) protect against hardware/rack power failures.

questions.title: CS1: TF - Entra ID Global Scope
questions.prompt: True or False: Azure Entra ID (Azure AD) is a Regional service tied to a single physical datacenter building.
questions.explanation: False. Azure Entra ID is a Global service not bound to a single Azure region.

questions.title: CS1: TF - Bicep Compilation
questions.prompt: True or False: Microsoft Bicep files compile directly into native ARM JSON templates before deployment to Azure Resource Manager.
questions.explanation: True. Bicep is a transparent syntax abstraction that transpiles into ARM JSON templates.
